observation_summary: The Joda-Time library incorrectly calculates the UTC offset during a Daylight Saving Time (DST) transition in the Moscow time zone. Specifically, for local times during the autumn overlap, the library returns an offset of +03:00 instead of the expected +04:00.
reasoning_summary: The failure occurs during the calculation of the offset from a local time during a DST transition. This is a procedural calculation issue where the logic for determining the correct offset based on the local time input is flawed. It is not a missing guard (Checking), a simple wrong constant (Assignment), or a design-level capability gap (Function/Class/Object). It is a flaw in the computational strategy used to resolve the local time to an offset, which is characteristic of an Algorithm/Method defect.
evidence_gaps: The actual implementation code for DateTimeZone.getOffsetFromLocal is not provided in the snippets, only the test code and abstract class definitions.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the issue involves a transition boundary, the failure is in the resulting calculation of the offset, not just a missing check for the boundary condition.
The issue is localized to the calculation of the offset for a given local time, rather than a broken association between two distinct objects or structures.
